root_cause.text: In the Bluetooth L2CAP reconfiguration path, `l2cap_config_req()` incorrectly treated an already-connected ERTM/streaming channel like a fresh setup and re-ran `l2cap_ertm_init()`/`l2cap_chan_ready()`, causing resource reinitialization without freeing existing queues/skbs, while `l2cap_parse_conf_req()` also allowed `remote_mps` to become zero, leading `l2cap_segment_sdu()` to compute a zero `pdu_len` and loop forever.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (chan->state != BT_CONNECTED)` around the `l2cap_ertm_init()` and `l2cap_chan_ready()` calls in `l2cap_config_req()`, matching the description that reconfiguration in `BT_CONNECTED` was falling through to double-init and leaking `tx_q`, `srej_q`, `srej_list`, `retrans_list`, and `chan->sdu`; it also adds `if (!pdu_len) return -EINVAL;` in `l2cap_segment_sdu()`, confirming that a zero `remote_mps`/`pdu_len` path previously caused a non-terminating segmentation loop.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject zero-length PDU sizing in l2cap_segment_sdu() by returning -EINVAL before segmentation proceeds.
intent_record.what: In l2cap_segment_sdu(), a new early return was added: if the computed pdu_len is zero, the function now returns -EINVAL before any SDU segmentation logic runs.
intent_record.how: This prevents the code from continuing with an invalid zero-length PDU size, which would otherwise lead to incorrect segmentation behavior or unsafe calculations. At runtime, the function now fails fast when no usable PDU length is available.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid rerunning ERTM/Streaming setup and ready/disconnect handling once the L2CAP channel is already connected.
intent_record.what: The patch wraps the existing ERTM/Streaming initialization and subsequent error/ready handling inside a new `if (chan->state != BT_CONNECTED)` check within the `CONF_INPUT_DONE` path. Previously, `set_default_fcs(chan)` was always followed by optional `l2cap_ertm_init(chan)`, then either `l2cap_send_disconn_req()` or `l2cap_chan_ready()`; now all of that logic is skipped when the channel state is `BT_CONNECTED`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, once the channel is already in `BT_CONNECTED` state, this code no longer reinitializes ERTM/Streaming parameters and no longer attempts to transition the channel to ready or disconnect based on that initialization result. This prevents duplicate or inappropriate post-configuration handling after the channel has already become connected, avoiding state-machine races or redundant setup/teardown.

grouping_result.intent: Reject zero-length PDU sizing in l2cap_segment_sdu() by returning -EINVAL before segmentation proceeds.
Avoid rerunning ERTM/Streaming setup and ready/disconnect handling once the L2CAP channel is already connected.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses one part of the root cause: it prevents zero `pdu_len` / zero-length PDU sizing in `l2cap_segment_sdu()`, which was caused by `remote_mps` becoming zero and led to the infinite loop.

The group directly matches the first part of the root cause: it prevents l2cap_config_req() from treating an already-connected ERTM/streaming channel like a fresh setup and rerunning initialization/ready handling, which addresses the resource reinitialization problem.

candidates.rationale: This line allows `pdu_len` to become zero when `remote_mps` is zero, which directly triggers the zero-length segmentation path and can cause `l2cap_segment_sdu()` to loop forever.

This conditional enters the reconfiguration completion path even when the channel is already connected, which is the gateway to incorrectly rerunning setup logic on an established ERTM/streaming channel.
Reinitializing ERTM/streaming state here on an already-connected channel is the direct faulty behavior that can recreate internal resources without properly releasing the existing ones.
Marking the channel ready again after rerunning setup on an already-connected channel contributes to the incorrect reconfiguration flow described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional allows the reconfiguration completion path to run even when the channel is already connected, which is the entry point for incorrectly re-running setup logic on an established ERTM/streaming channel.
This reinitializes ERTM state during reconfiguration on an already-connected channel, which can recreate internal queues/resources without properly freeing the existing ones.
Marking the channel ready again after rerunning setup contributes to the incorrect reconfiguration flow that treats an established channel like a fresh one.
If remote_mps is zero, this line makes pdu_len zero, which triggers the zero-length segmentation path and can cause l2cap_segment_sdu() to loop forever.
